articles.title: It Has to Go Out Before Four
articles.summary: The training files must finish uploading and validation before 16:00, but the speaker’s job title changes at the last minute. Su Ning has updated all three files; she still needs all six signatures on the green change form before she can submit them.
storyParagraphs: At 15:10 on Thursday, Su Ning has packaged the handbook, name badges, and sign-in sheet for the next day’s client training. The print shop requires the files to finish uploading and automated validation before 16:00, and the upload and validation together normally take eight to ten minutes. Just as she is about to submit it, the speaker emails to say that their job title has just changed. The agenda cover, name badge, and front-desk sign-in page all display that title.

The office uses a green change form under which every last-minute change must be confirmed in sequence by content, front desk, venue, catering, technical support, and finance. The rule originally dealt with changes such as time, headcount, or floor location, where one change can affect several areas at once. Su Ning updates the three files; the content owner checks the handbook and badge, and front desk checks the sign-in page. Venue and catering quickly write “no impact,” but the technical colleague is in the equipment room, so the paper form stops at the fifth line.

While waiting, Su Ning checks the full set of event outputs again. The room booking contains no job title, the catering list contains only headcount, the technical run sheet lists equipment and time slots, and the quotation contains no speaker name. She writes the three checked outputs—“handbook / badge / sign-in page”—on the back of the green form and keeps the four unaffected documents beside it on the desk, still waiting for technical support and finance to sign.

The technical colleague returns sometime after 15:40 and signs, and finance then confirms that the cost is unchanged. All six confirmations are not complete until 15:53. Even if Su Ning starts uploading immediately, there is not enough time to finish the eight-to-ten-minute upload and validation before 16:00. The print shop keeps the job for the next morning’s first print run but cancels delivery. Su Ning goes to the shop at 07:00 the next day to collect two boxes of materials before heading back to the training venue.

After the event, the supervisor and the six role owners spread the green form on the table and write “affected outputs” at the top. Whoever raises a change first marks the handbook, badge, sign-in page, or other output that may change, and the corresponding owner signs beside it. Uncertain effects are left for the event coordinator to add another owner. Changes to time, location, headcount, or other items that affect several functions still default to a multi-party route through venue, catering, front desk, technical support, and other relevant roles.

Before the next training submission, the client changes one letter in an attendee’s surname. Su Ning marks “name badge / sign-in sheet.” The content owner checks the displayed name, and front desk checks the sign-in page. She starts the upload at 15:22, and validation finishes at 15:31. She places the confirmed badge PDF into the print package and continues packing the next day’s sign-in materials.
articles.overall: Coordination cost comes from the communication, waiting, confirmation, and integration required among interdependent tasks. Full-team confirmation can be reasonable for highly connected changes, but extra waiting appears when the coordination route includes roles with no actual dependency on a particular change.
explanationParagraphs: The title change affected only the handbook, badge, and sign-in page, yet the old process waited for six roles. Confirmation finished at 15:53, leaving too little time for the required 8–10 minutes of upload and validation before 16:00, so delivery was lost.

The revised form asks the initiator to mark potential effects; content and front desk still check their own files, and the coordinator can add a missed owner. It reduces waiting at roles unaffected by that change, while retaining multi-party confirmation for changes to time, location, headcount, and other connected work.

module.intro: Start with the outputs that a change actually enters, then decide who must confirm and who can add missed dependencies.
module.diagramTitle: How a Title Change Moves from Six-Station Waiting to Dependency-Based Routing
diagramSteps: Receive the change and update the directly affected files
Run the old six-role sequential confirmation
Check whether the change actually enters each role’s output
Miss the workable upload-and-validation window because of waiting
Use the affected-output route on a later real task
diagramStepNotes: The title appears in the handbook, badge, and sign-in page.
Venue and catering mark no impact, while the paper form waits at technical support.
Su Ning confirms that room, catering, technical, and pricing documents contain no title field.
Confirmation finishes at 15:53, leaving insufficient time for 8–10 minutes of upload and validation before 16:00.
A later surname change is confirmed only by content and front desk; upload starts at 15:22 and validation finishes at 15:31.
mapping: Green change form → the original coordination mechanism.
Three output names on the back → the concrete dependency relationship.
07:00 collection the next morning → the visible cost of mismatched waiting.
Affected-output field + coordinator’s add-on authority → reduced waiting while preserving dependency checks.
module.boundary: Coordination cost does not mean that fewer confirmations are always better. Changes involving shared resources, time, location, or headcount still require multi-party coordination. The initiator can also miss an impact, so owner confirmation and coordinator add-on authority preserve necessary coordination cost.
module.reflection: If the initiator can only identify what is “possibly affected,” how would you design owner confirmation and add-on rules to reduce irrelevant waiting without missing real dependencies?

references.citation: Malone, T. W., & Crowston, K. (1994). The Interdisciplinary Study of Coordination. ACM Computing Surveys, 26(1), 87–119.
references.use: Supports understanding organizational coordination in terms of dependencies among activities, coordination mechanisms, and coordination costs; different dependencies may require different mechanisms.

references.citation: Crowston, K. (1997). A Coordination Theory Approach to Organizational Process Design. Organization Science, 8(2), 157–175.
references.use: Supports process-design reasoning that compares coordination mechanisms based on task and resource dependencies; a single case is not treated as a universal causal law.

articles.summaryZh: 培训资料必须在16:00前完成上传和校验，主讲人的头衔却在最后一刻变了。三个文件已经改好，苏宁仍要等绿色变更单上的六处签字齐全，才能提交。
storyParagraphsZh: 周四下午三点十分，苏宁把第二天客户培训的手册、胸牌和签到表打包好。印厂要求16:00前完成文件上传和自动校验，平时整包上传和校验要八到十分钟。就在她准备提交时，主讲人来信说职位头衔刚更新。议程封面、胸牌和前台签到页都显示这行字。
办公室沿用的绿色变更单要求所有临时修改都由内容、前台、场地、餐饮、技术和财务依次确认。这个规则原本常处理时间、人数、楼层等一改就牵动多处的事项。苏宁先改好三个文件，内容负责人核过手册和胸牌，前台核过签到页。场地和餐饮很快写“无影响”，技术同事却正在机房，纸单停在第五栏。
等候时，苏宁把整套活动输出重新对了一遍：房间预订不含头衔，餐饮名单只有人数，技术运行表只有设备和时段，报价也没有讲师姓名。她把已核过的“手册／胸牌／签到页”写在绿色单背面，连同那四份没有头衔字段的文件留在桌边，继续等技术和财务签字。
技术同事三点四十多回来签字，财务随后确认费用不变。绿色单到三点五十三才完成全部六处；即使立刻开始上传，也来不及在16:00前完成八到十分钟的上传和校验。印厂保留次日早班印刷，但不再安排配送，苏宁第二天七点去门店自取两箱资料，再赶回培训现场。
活动后，主管和六个负责人把绿色单摊在桌上，在表头写下“受影响输出”。发起人先勾出可能改动的手册、胸牌、签到页等输出，旁边由对应负责人签字；拿不准的地方留给活动协调人补加负责人。时间、地点、人数等会牵动多环节的变更，仍默认走场地、餐饮、前台、技术等多方确认路线。
下一场培训临近提交时，客户把一名参会者姓氏改了一个字母。苏宁勾选“胸牌／签到”，内容负责人核显示名，前台核签到页，三点二十二分她开始上传，三点三十一分校验完成。她把确认过的胸牌PDF放进打印包，继续装第二天的签到材料。
articles.overallZh: 协调成本来自相互依赖任务之间所需的沟通、等待、确认与整合。旧的全员确认在高关联变更中合理，但当协调路径覆盖没有实际依赖的岗位时，会增加额外等待。
explanationParagraphsZh: 头衔变更只进入手册、胸牌和签到页，却按旧规则等待六岗位，15:53才完成确认，已不足以在16:00前完成8–10分钟上传校验，因此失去配送。
新表让发起人标潜在影响，内容和前台仍须核对各自文件，协调人也能补加遗漏的负责人。减少的是不涉及本次改动的等待；时间、地点、人数等高关联变更仍保留多方确认。

moduleZh.intro: 从一项变更真正进入哪些输出开始，再决定谁必须确认以及谁有权补加依赖。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 头衔变更怎样从六站等待变成按依赖路由
diagramSteps: 收到变更并修改直接受影响的文件
旧流程仍按六岗位顺序确认
核对变更是否实际进入各岗位输出
因等待错过可完成上传校验的时间窗
后续任务按受影响输出完成真实路由
diagramStepNotes: 头衔实际出现在手册、胸牌和签到页。
场地、餐饮签无影响，纸单在技术岗位等待。
苏宁核对房间、餐饮、技术和费用文件均无头衔字段。
15:53完成确认，已不足以在16:00前完成8–10分钟上传校验。
后续姓氏变更只经内容和前台确认，15:22上传、15:31校验完成。
mapping: 绿色变更单 → 原协调机制。
背面三份输出名称 → 具体依赖关系。
次日07:00自取 → 不匹配等待造成的可见代价。
受影响输出栏＋协调人补加权 → 缩减等待同时保留依赖确认。
moduleZh.boundary: 协调成本不意味着确认越少越好。共享资源、时间、地点、人数等高关联变更仍需要多方协调；发起人也可能漏判影响，因此对应负责人确认和协调人补加仍保留必要成本。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果发起人只能先判断“可能受影响”，你会怎样设计负责人确认和补加机制，既减少无关等待又避免漏掉真实依赖？

referencesZh.citation: Malone, T. W., & Crowston, K. (1994). The Interdisciplinary Study of Coordination. ACM Computing Surveys, 26(1), 87–119.
referencesZh.use: 支持从活动间依赖、协调机制与协调成本角度理解组织协调；不同依赖可需要不同机制。

referencesZh.citation: Crowston, K. (1997). A Coordination Theory Approach to Organizational Process Design. Organization Science, 8(2), 157–175.
referencesZh.use: 支持从任务和资源依赖出发比较不同协调机制的过程设计思路；不把单一案例写成普遍因果定律。

articles.title: The Brake Rotors on the Shelf
articles.summary: After switching to deliveries every two weeks, Mira hears that three repair shops are waiting for stock. The next purchase order is still unsent.
articles.summaryZh: 补货单改成两周一批后，米拉收到了三家维修店等货的消息，下一张采购单还没发出。
storyParagraphs: In the first week of April, Mira spread the replenishment order for the current quarter for the e-bike brake-rotor category across the warehouse desk. For that same category and using the same cost basis, first-quarter opening inventory was €15,000, closing inventory was €9,000, and cost of goods sold for the quarter was €48,000. She wanted to reduce the amount of cash tied up in stock, so she used a simple opening-and-closing average as an approximation: average inventory €12,000, giving first-quarter inventory turnover of €48,000 ÷ €12,000 = 4 times.

Mira wrote 90 ÷ 4 ≈ 22.5 days in the corner of the first-quarter report, using 90 days for this calculation. She placed the supplier’s normal lead time and everyday demand for the common sizes beside the replenishment order, selecting this category for a limited trial. The large monthly batch on the original order became a delivery every two weeks; slow-moving sizes were reduced first, and fast-moving sizes were also trimmed by one layer. She sent out the April trial order and left the first-quarter turnover of 4 on the old report.

After two weeks of the trial, warehouse occupancy was indeed lower, but the two most common sizes each went out of stock for two days. An urgent order from the repair shop North Bridge Cycles had to wait that day, and two other repair shops also faced delays. One of them bought elsewhere rather than risk postponing a customer handover. Mira had been about to cut the next order again, but stopped her pen when she saw the lost purchase and the three waiting orders.

She kept the two-week cycle but raised the minimum stock level for the two fast-moving sizes, while leaving the slower sizes at the lower quantities. Using the same cost basis, she re-totaled the revised purchase order and estimated that the inventory investment would still be lower than under the old monthly-batch plan, but she no longer reduced every size by the same proportion. Supplier lead time stayed as written on the order, but she added stock back for the two fast-moving sizes.

At month-end review, Mira still kept the Q1 turnover of 4 and the 22.5-day figure on the first page. Beside them she recorded that each of the two sizes had been out of stock for two days, three repair shops had waited, one had bought elsewhere, along with margins by size and supplier lead time. She also reviewed several in-week inventory snapshots because the €12,000 average based only on €15,000 opening and €9,000 closing inventory could not show the movement in between. The write-off field was still blank; she left it to be completed after the stock check.

Before placing the next order, Mira rewrote the minimum stock levels for the two fast-moving brake rotors on their shelf cards. The purchase order still said “every two weeks,” but one fast-moving quantity she had previously cut was added back by one layer.
storyParagraphsZh: 四月第一周，米拉把电助力车刹车碟这一品类的这一季度补货单摊在仓库桌上。第一季度同一品类、同一成本口径下，期初库存15,000欧元、期末9,000欧元，同期销售成本48,000欧元。她想少压一些库存资金，于是先用期初期末简单平均作近似：平均12,000，第一季度周转48,000÷12,000=4次。
米拉在第一季度报表页角写下90÷4≈22.5天，暂按90天作这次换算。她又把供应商正常交期和常用规格的日常需求放到补货单旁，选出这一品类作小范围试行。原单上每月一次的大批量被改成两周一批，慢动规格先减量，快销规格也暂时压低一层。她发出了这张四月试行单，把第一季度的4次周转留在旧报表上。
试行两周后，仓库占用确实下降，但两个最常用规格分别各断货两天。维修店“北桥车房”的急单当天只能等，另外两家维修店也遇到延迟，其中一家为了不耽误交车，临时转去别家采购。米拉原本正准备继续减少下一批数量，看到转购记录和三个等待订单后，把笔停在采购单上。
她保留两周一批，却把两个快销规格的最低库存线往上调，慢动规格仍维持较低数量。她按同一成本口径重新汇总新版采购单，预计占用库存资金仍低于原来的月批量方案，但不再让所有规格按同一幅度下降。供应商交期仍照旧写在单上，两个快销规格的数量却被她加了回来。
月底复盘时，米拉仍把第一季度4次周转和22.5天留在首页，同时并列记录两个规格各两天缺货、三家维修店等待、一家转购、各规格毛利和供应交期。她又补看了几次周内库存快照，因为只用期初15,000和期末9,000得到的12,000平均数看不到中间波动。报废一栏还空着，她留待清点确认后再填。
下一次下单前，米拉把两个快销刹车碟的最低库存线重新写到货架卡上。采购单仍标着“两周一批”，其中一个原本被删减的快销数量被加回一层。
explanationParagraphs: Inventory turnover is commonly calculated as cost of goods sold for a period divided by average inventory measured at cost for the same period. Here, only the Q1 e-bike brake-rotor category is used: €48,000 ÷ [(€15,000 + €9,000)/2] = 4 times. Using 90 days for the calculation, inventory days are about 90 ÷ 4 = 22.5 days.

An opening-and-closing average is only an approximation. It does not prove actual turnover after the April trial and cannot determine replenishment frequency on its own. Turnover changes must be viewed alongside stockouts, lead time, margin, write-offs, and service levels.
explanationParagraphsZh: 库存周转通常用同期间销售成本÷成本计价平均库存。本例只看Q1电助力车刹车碟品类：48,000÷[(15,000＋9,000)/2]＝4次；按演算90天计算，库存天数约90÷4＝22.5天。
期初期末平均只是近似，不能证明四月试行后的真实周转，也不能单独决定补货频率。周转变化必须和缺货、交期、毛利、报废及服务水平一起观察。
articles.overall: Inventory turnover relates cost of goods sold to average inventory over the same period. It helps assess cash tied up, while replenishment decisions also depend on size-level demand, lead time, and stockouts: one less layer of stock may mean another day of waiting for a customer.
articles.overallZh: 库存周转把同期间销售成本与平均库存放在一起。它能帮助检查资金占用，补货决定还要结合规格需求、交期和缺货：少留一层货，可能也意味着让客户多等一天。

module.intro: Inventory turnover should be calculated with data from the same period, category, and cost basis. A historical ratio can help motivate a replenishment trial, but it cannot by itself prove that a new plan is faster or better.
module.diagramTitle: How Q1 turnover feeds into a limited replenishment trial
diagramSteps: Fix the same category, period, and cost basis
Approximate average inventory from opening and closing inventory
Calculate Q1 turnover and approximate inventory days
Use cash tied up, lead time, and demand to run a limited trial
Use stockouts and service outcomes to revise the next purchase order
diagramStepNotes: Q1 covers only the e-bike brake-rotor category: cost of goods sold €48,000, opening inventory €15,000, and closing inventory €9,000, all measured at cost.
Average inventory ≈ (€15,000 + €9,000)/2 = €12,000; the two-point average is only a simplified approximation.
€48,000/€12,000 = 4 times; using 90 days, 90/4 = 22.5 days. This describes Q1 only.
Mira combines that figure with cash tied up, normal lead time, and size-level demand to trial two-week replenishment rather than translating turnover of 4 directly into an “optimal two weeks.”
After the two fast-moving sizes are each out of stock for two days, she raises their minimum levels and continues tracking stockouts, lead time, margins, write-offs, and inventory snapshots.
mapping: €48,000 cost of goods sold → Q1 turnover numerator for the brake-rotor category.
€15,000 and €9,000 → opening and closing inventory for the same category at cost.
4 times and 22.5 days → approximate Q1 historical turnover and inventory days, not April trial results.
Each of two sizes out of stock for two days → visible service cost of the small-batch trial.
Higher minimum level for fast movers → restored buffer while keeping the two-week cycle.
module.boundary: Inventory turnover should not substitute sales revenue for cost of goods sold, and a low inventory figure on one day should not stand for an entire period. Opening-and-closing average inventory is only an approximation; when inventory fluctuates materially, more observation points are needed. Higher turnover can coincide with stockouts, expediting costs, or margin changes. Write-offs should also be tracked, but when no actual write-off result exists it should not be assumed to be zero or treated as evidence of improvement.
module.reflection: If next quarter’s turnover rises but stockouts of fast-moving sizes and customer purchases elsewhere also increase, which inventory buffers would you keep?

moduleZh.intro: 库存周转要用同一期间、同一品类、同一成本口径的数据计算；得到的历史比率可以帮助提出补货试验，但不能直接证明新方案更快或更优。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: Q1周转率怎样进入一次小范围补货试行
diagramSteps: 锁定同一品类、期间和成本口径
用期初期末库存近似平均库存
计算Q1周转率和演算库存天数
结合资金占用、交期与需求做小范围试行
用缺货与服务结果修正下一张采购单
diagramStepNotes: Q1仅看电助力车刹车碟：销售成本48,000，期初15,000、期末9,000，均按成本计价。
米拉据此结合资金占用、正常交期与规格需求，试行两周一批，而非把4次直接转换成“最优两周”。
两个快销规格分别各断货两天后，她提高最低库存线，并继续跟踪缺货、交期、毛利、报废和库存快照。
mapping: 48,000欧元销售成本 → Q1该刹车碟品类的周转分子。
15,000与9,000欧元 → 同品类期初期末成本库存。
4次与22.5天 → Q1历史周转近似，不是四月试行结果。
两个规格各断货两天 → 小批量试行的可见服务代价。
提高快销最低线 → 在保留两周补货的同时恢复缓冲。
moduleZh.boundary: 库存周转不能用销售收入替代销售成本，也不能用某一日低库存代表整个期间。期初期末平均只是近似，波动明显时需要更多观察点。更高周转可能伴随缺货、加急成本或毛利变化；报废也应跟踪，但没有实绩时不能假定为零或当作改善证据。

articles.title: Four Filter Cartridges Spill onto the Overflow Rack
articles.summary: Sales of Type A water-filter cartridges rise by only four units for one week, yet the next delivery contains twenty-eight. Xu Cen puts four on the temporary overflow rack and traces the replenishment rule that produced the order.
storyParagraphs: Before opening on Monday of Week 3, the upstream warehouse delivers 28 Type A water-filter cartridges. The store’s main shelf can hold at most 40 units, and 16 are still on hand before the delivery. Once all 28 arrive, on-hand inventory becomes 44, so four have to go onto the overflow rack beside it. Customers bought only 24 the previous week. Xu Cen worries that the replenishment sheet may be wrong and brings the delivery note and the previous weeks’ records to the store manager.

The store has been using the same simplified policy throughout. Lead time is fixed at one week, and each week begins with the full arrival of the previous week’s order. There are no backorders. At the end of each week, the store forecasts the next week using the average of the two most recent actual sales figures and replenishes inventory position to twice that forecast. Inventory position equals on-hand inventory plus outstanding orders not yet received minus backorders. Before Week 1, on-hand inventory is 40, pipeline inventory is 0, backorders are 0, and the two earlier weeks both had sales of 20.

After selling 20 in Week 1, on-hand inventory falls to 20. The forecast remains 20 and the target inventory position is 40, so the store orders 20 at the end of the week. Those 20 arrive at the start of Week 2, restoring on-hand inventory to 40. Week 2 sales are 24, leaving 16. The average of the two most recent weeks, 20 and 24, becomes 22, so the target inventory position rises from 40 to 44.

Before the Week 2 order is placed, pipeline inventory and backorders are both zero, so target 44 minus on-hand 16 gives an order of 28. Xu Cen separates it into two parts: 24 replace what was sold that week, while another four reflect the target inventory position rising from 40 to 44. Once the order is placed, inventory position returns to 44. At the start of Week 3, all 28 arrive: 16 + 28 = 44, with 40 on the main shelf and four on the overflow rack in front of her.

In Week 3, customers buy 20, leaving 24 on hand. The average of sales 24 and 20 is still 22, so the target remains 44 and the store orders 20. The main shelf can now hold all remaining stock, and Xu Cen moves the four cartridges off the overflow rack. The manager begins sending upstream two separate columns—final customer sales and store orders—while leaving the replenishment formula unchanged for now.

In Week 4, the 20 ordered units arrive at the start of the week, bringing on-hand inventory to 44. Customers buy 24, leaving 20. The forecast remains 22, so the store orders 24. Across the four weeks, customer sales are 20, 24, 20, 24, while store orders are 20, 28, 20, 24. Xu Cen copies the two columns onto the replenishment sheet, with the delivery note for 28 still clipped behind the records.
articles.overall: The bullwhip effect refers to upstream order variability exceeding final-demand variability for the same product over the same periods. This example uses only demand-signal processing and forecast updating: the store updates its forecast from sales, and its order both replaces units sold and adds stock to meet the higher target, amplifying the order.
explanationParagraphs: Week 2 sales of 24 raise the forecast from 20 to 22 and the target inventory position from 40 to 44. Before ordering, on-hand inventory is 16, pipeline and backorders are zero, and inventory position is 16. The order is 44 − 16 = 28: 24 replaces sales and four raises the target.

For the same four weeks, sales variance is 4 and order variance is 11, a ratio of 11 / 4 = 2.75. The fifth diagram note shows the calculation. This ratio describes only these four weeks and cannot establish a long-run pattern.
Sharing final sales helps the warehouse distinguish customer demand from store orders, but the store still orders under its original forecast rule; amplification does not automatically disappear.

module.intro: Hold the product and weekly periods fixed, and track on-hand inventory, pipeline inventory, sales, forecast, target inventory position, and orders separately.
diagramSteps: Start with on-hand 40, pipeline 0, and backorders 0
Sell 20 in Week 1 and order 20
Receive 20 in Week 2, sell 24, and raise the forecast to 22
Subtract on-hand 16 from target 44 to get an order of 28
Continue for two more weeks and compare variability over the same four periods
diagramStepNotes: Before Week 1, the two previous sales figures are both 20, so forecast = 20 and target inventory position = 40.
At the end of Week 1, on-hand inventory is 20 and pipeline is 0, so the store orders 20.
At the start of Week 2, on-hand is 40; after selling 24, 16 remain; forecast = (20 + 24) / 2 = 22.
Before ordering, pipeline and backorders are zero, so inventory position is 16. Then 44 − 16 = 28: 24 replaces sales and four raises the target; next week 16 + 28 = 44.

Across four weeks, mean sales = 22 and variance = (4 + 4 + 4 + 4) / 4 = 4; mean orders = 23 and variance = (9 + 25 + 9 + 1) / 4 = 11. The ratio is 11 / 4 = 2.75. Variance averages squared differences from each series mean; ranges 4 and 8 are visual aids only.
mapping: Four cartridges on the overflow rack → space occupied by stock above the earlier 40-unit target after the target rises.
Two-week moving average → the only demand-signal-processing mechanism used here.
Order of 28 → the combined result of replacing sales and raising the target.
Separate sales/order columns → allows the upstream warehouse to distinguish final demand from store ordering.
module.boundary: This original simplified policy shows forecast updating over only four weeks. It includes no promotions, minimum batch orders, rationing games, or stockouts. Variance compares variability over the same four periods; range is only a visual aid. These numbers do not establish a long-run pattern. Sharing sales can reduce information distortion, but amplification may remain if the store’s rule is unchanged.
module.reflection: When an order of 28 appears while sales were only 24, how would you separate the “replace 24” component from the “extra 4” caused by the higher target so that an order jump is not mistaken for a demand jump?

references.use: Supports the research framework on how forecasting, lead times, and demand information affect order variability, and how sharing demand information may reduce but not necessarily eliminate amplification; the story numbers are original simplified conditions.

articles.summaryZh: A型滤芯一周只多卖了四个，下一周却送来二十八个。许岑把四个放上临时周转架，随后沿着补货规则追出这张订单是怎么来的。
storyParagraphsZh: 第三周周一开店前，上游仓库送来28个A型净水滤芯。门店主货位最多放40个，送货前店里还剩16个，因此28个全到后在手变成44，四个只能先放到旁边的周转架。上一周顾客只买了24个，许岑担心补货表算错，把送货单和前几周记录拿到店长桌上。
门店一直使用同一套简化政策：供货期固定一周，每周周初上周订单全数到店；没有欠交。周末用最近两周实际销量的平均数预测下一周，并把库存位置补到预测的两倍。库存位置等于在手库存加已下单未到货，再减欠交。第一周开始前，在手40、在途0、欠交0；此前两周销量都为20。
第一周卖20后在手20，预测仍为20，目标库存位置40，所以周末订20。第二周周初这20个全到，在手回到40；当周卖24后剩16。最近两周销量20和24的平均变成22，目标库存位置从40提高到44。
第二周末下单前，在途和欠交都为0，所以用目标44减在手16，得到订单28。许岑把它拆开：24个补回当周卖掉的数量，另外4个来自目标库存位置从40升到44。订单下出后库存位置回到44；第三周周初28个全到，16＋28＝44，也就是她眼前40个进主货位、4个上周转架的状态。
第三周顾客买走20个，在手降到24；最近两周24和20的平均仍为22，目标44，因此订20。主货位已经能容下余货，许岑把周转架上的四个移回去。店长把终端销量和门店订单分成两列同步给上游，补货公式暂时没改。
到了第四周，周初这20个到货后在手44，顾客买24后剩20，预测仍为22，于是订24。四周顾客销量是20、24、20、24，门店订单则是20、28、20、24。许岑把这两列抄到补货表上，那张28个的送货单继续夹在记录后面。
articles.overallZh: 牛鞭效应指同一商品、同一期间口径下，上游订单波动大于终端需求波动。本篇只采用需求信号处理与预测更新：门店把销量变化用于更新预测，订货既补回卖掉的数量，也补足上调的库存目标，放大了订单。
explanationParagraphsZh: 第二周销量24使两周均值预测由20升至22，目标库存位置由40升至44。下单前在手16、在途0、欠交0，库存位置也是16，所以订单为44－16＝28：24补销售，4补目标上调。
同四周销量总体方差为4，订单为11，方差比11÷4＝2.75；第五步图注可复算。这个比值只描述本例四周，不能推成长期规律。
共享终端销量帮助上游区分顾客需求与门店订货，但门店仍按原预测规则下单，放大不会因此自动消失。

articles.title: The Same Saturday Pass
articles.summary: The front desk is waiting to print the sign: should the same Saturday pass stay at €10 for everyone, or become €12 standard and €7 for students?
articles.summaryZh: 前台等着印价牌：同一张周六通行证，要继续统一10欧元，还是改成标准12、学生7欧元？
storyParagraphs: On Wednesday afternoon, Irene had to send the day-pass page for the next two Saturdays live by Thursday, while the front desk was also waiting to print the new price sign. The space had 90 places, and every day pass included the same opening hours, workbench, and basic tools. Nearby substitutes were limited, giving the space some pricing discretion. Everyone had previously paid a uniform €10, and she did not want to lower the price for everyone simply to fill empty places when some visitors were already willing to pay €10.

She and a colleague used the same scenario demand relationship to forecast both pricing options. If the uniform €10 price stayed, they predicted 45 regular visitors and 25 students, for 70 passes and €700 of revenue. The listed variable cost was €2 per entrant for both groups, so forecast contribution was €700 - 70 × €2 = €560. The 70 passes and €560 were forecast baseline figures, not sales that had already occurred.

The second page showed a standard price of €12 and a student price of €7. Under the same demand relationship, changing prices was forecast to reduce regular visitors to 40 and raise students to 35, for 75 passes in total. Revenue would be 40 × €12 + 35 × €7 = €725; subtracting the listed €150 of variable cost, 75 × €2, gave forecast contribution of €575. Irene circled the €15 difference and noted beside it that both columns deducted only €2 per person; fixed facility costs and any additional verification time had not been included.

Irene selected the segmented-price option and entered a trial period of just two Saturdays. The existing ticketing process already had named QR codes and student-status checks; after checking it, she kept transfer disabled so lower-priced passes could not simply be resold to someone else. She stated on the page that both passes included the same workbench, tools, and opening hours, then handed the €12 standard / €7 student sign to the front desk. The old €10 sign was set aside.

On the first Saturday morning, a regular visitor who had always bought the €10 pass chose not to enter after seeing €12. He asked at the desk, “If the workbench and tools are the same, why am I paying 12 while students pay 7?” At the same time, student-pass sales were higher than before. Irene recorded his decision not to buy, the fairness concern, and actual ticket sales in the day’s operating record instead of substituting the forecast €575 for the real outcome.

After closing, Irene did not permanently laminate the new price sign. She slipped it back into the front-desk folder and wrote “test one more Saturday” in the upper-right corner. The old uniform €10 sign was still lying on the desk, and the transfer button on the named-ticket page remained disabled.
storyParagraphsZh: 周三下午，艾琳要在周四前把接下来两个周六的创客空间日票页面送去上线，前台也等着打印新价牌。空间有90个位置，所有日票使用相同开放时间、工作台和基础工具；附近替代选择有限，因此空间有一定定价余地。过去所有人统一10欧元，她不想为了填空位就把原本愿意付10欧元的人全部一起降价。
她和同事用同一套场景需求关系分别预测两个价格方案。若仍统一10欧元，预计普通访客45人、学生25人，共70张，收入700欧元；每位入场列出的可变成本都是2欧元，因此演算贡献为700－70×2＝560欧元。这些70张和560欧元都是预测基准，不是已经发生的售票结果。
另一版页面写成标准12欧元、学生7欧元。价格改变后，同一需求关系预测普通访客降到40人、学生升到35人，共75张；收入40×12＋35×7＝725欧元，扣列出的75×2＝150欧元可变成本后，演算贡献575欧元。艾琳圈出15欧元差额，又在旁边注明：两栏都只扣每人2欧元，场地固定费用和可能增加的核验工时尚未计入。
艾琳选了分组方案，试行期限只填两个周六。原有票务流程已有实名二维码和学生资格核对，她核查过后保留了关闭的转让按钮，低价票不能直接转给别人。她在页面上写明两种票使用相同工作台、工具和开放时间，将标准12欧元、学生7欧元的价牌交给前台，旧的10欧元牌子被放到一旁。
第一个周六上午，一位过去一直买10欧元日票的普通访客看到12欧元后没有进场。他问前台：“工位和工具都一样，为什么我现在12，学生是7？”与此同时，学生票销量比过去高。艾琳把他的放弃购买、这条价格公平质疑和当天实际售票一起记下，没有拿预测的575欧元替代真实结果。
关门后，艾琳没有把新价牌永久塑封，只把它夹回前台文件夹，右上角写着“再测一个周六”。旧的统一10欧元价牌仍放在桌上，实名票页面的转让按钮继续保持关闭。
explanationParagraphs: Price discrimination means charging different prices for comparable products or services when the difference cannot be fully explained by cost differences. It usually requires some pricing power and limits on resale between the differently priced groups.

In this example, the uniform €10 option has forecast contribution of €560, while the €12/€7 segmented option has forecast contribution of €575. Both subtract only the listed €2 variable cost per entrant, so neither is complete profit; the demand numbers are scenario forecasts rather than observed results.
explanationParagraphsZh: 价格歧视指对可比产品或服务收取不同价格，而价格差不能由成本差充分解释。它通常需要一定定价空间，并要求不同价格之间的转售受到限制。
本例统一10欧元方案预测贡献560；12/7欧元分组方案预测贡献575。两者只扣列出的每人2欧元可变成本，并非完整利润；需求数字也只是场景演算，不是实测。
articles.overall: When identifiable groups pay different prices for the same service, examine whether costs explain the difference and whether lower-priced access can be resold. Forecast sales and contribution for two options are only estimates; the decision also needs additional costs, customer feedback, and accessibility.
articles.overallZh: 同一服务按可识别群体收取不同价格时，需要看价格差是否由成本解释，以及低价能否转售。两种方案的销量和贡献只是预测，实际决定还要查看额外费用、顾客反馈和可及性。

module.intro: Segmented pricing requires comparable service, a price difference not fully explained by cost, some pricing discretion, and a way to limit simple resale from the lower-priced group to the higher-priced group. Actual demand still has to validate the business result.

Hold the listed unit variable cost equal across groups

diagramStepNotes: Every pass includes the same opening hours, workbench, and basic tools, with 90 places available.
The listed variable cost is €2 per entrant for both groups, so that cost does not explain the €12 versus €7 price difference.
At a uniform €10, the forecast is 45 regular visitors and 25 students, 70 passes total; revenue €700 and contribution €700 - €140 = €560.
At €12/€7, the forecast is 40 regular visitors and 35 students, 75 passes total; revenue €725 and contribution €725 - €150 = €575. Fixed costs and any extra verification labor are excluded.
Named QR codes and status checks limit resale; on the first Saturday a regular visitor declines to buy and raises a fairness concern, so the second Saturday still has to be tested.
mapping: Old uniform €10 sign → forecast baseline pricing option.
€12 standard / €7 student page → segmented prices for the same service.

module.boundary: Student status is only an identifiable grouping variable; it does not prove identical willingness to pay within the group. The demand figures are scenario assumptions, and actual sales may differ. The €560 and €575 figures subtract only the listed unit variable cost, so fixed costs and any incremental verification cost require separate consideration. Real-world use also depends on actual market power, resale conditions, fairness and accessibility, and applicable rules; this story does not claim that a particular practice is necessarily legal or illegal. Only two options are compared here; no optimal price has been established.
module.reflection: If actual contribution on the second Saturday still falls short of the forecast €575 but seat utilization rises, which additional costs and customer reactions would you examine before keeping the segmented prices?

560与575欧元 → 两种预测方案的贡献，不是完整利润或实测结果。
未永久塑封的新价牌 → 两周测试尚未完成。
moduleZh.boundary: 学生身份只是可识别分组变量，不能证明组内每个人的支付意愿。演算需求只是场景假设，实际销量可能不同；560和575只扣列出的单位可变成本，固定费用和任何额外核验成本需另看。现实采用前还要结合市场力量、转售条件、公平与可及性以及适用规则，本故事不宣称某种做法当然合法或非法。这里只比较两个方案，并未求出最优价格。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果第二个周六的实际贡献没有达到预测575，但席位利用率提高，你还需要看哪些成本与顾客反应再决定是否保留分组价？

references.citation: Ellison, G. (2022). Industrial Organization I, Lecture 03: Price Discrimination, Part 1. MIT OpenCourseWare.
references.use: Supports charging different unit prices, grouping consumers, the role of market power, and constraints on resale.

referencesZh.citation: Ellison, G. (2022). Industrial Organization I, Lecture 03: Price Discrimination, Part 1. MIT OpenCourseWare.
referencesZh.use: 支持不同单位价格、消费者分组、市场力量与转售约束。

articles.title: The Clarinet That Sometimes Lost Its Low Note
articles.summary: A student clarinet returns to the repair room for a second time: the static check looks almost normal, but a low note still sometimes fails. Holding the leak light, Mia joins a senior technician in trying to reproduce this particular problem for the first time.
storyParagraphs: In her third week, a student clarinet comes back into Mia’s hands for the second time. Its tag reads, “Low note sometimes does not sound.” The newcomer uses a leak light to check the pad contact, but the static check shows no obvious continuous leak. She writes the positions checked on the repair sheet; that sheet alone cannot tell the school why the note sometimes fails.

For years, the district repair room has handled schools’ woodwind instruments together every Tuesday. Beside the long table, a shared log holds three technicians’ notes on return symptoms, interventions, and follow-up checks. Mia’s first-week assignment covered only leak checks. The senior technician responsible for the mechanism takes this clarinet’s repair sheet and asks her to repeat the key sequence described by the student. He watches the linkage from the other side while another technician records when anything unusual appears.

On the fifth repetition, one connecting key returns more slowly than on earlier attempts, and the leak light shows a thin line only at that moment. Based on this observation, the technician cleans and adjusts the linkage on this instrument. The three then repeat the movement and static check. The repair sheet says, “Observed this time: a thin line on the fifth repetition.” They copy the same entry into the shared log and ask the school to continue observing the instrument in use.

Over the next several weeks, Mia still begins with leak-light checks, but the shared repair log lets her see how existing staff have recorded cases that appear continuously versus only under particular movements. She combines the new entry for this clarinet with several older entries into a draft card: first try to reproduce the reported action, then record when the observation appears, and then hand the case to the relevant technician to decide the next step. The last section is left for the actual intervention and follow-up result.

The senior technician tries the draft card at the workbench and adds one exception: “If the static check already shows a clear continuous problem, hand it directly to the relevant technician; do not force a repetition of the reported movement.” Another technician later uses the card to mark the timing of a different intermittent problem and writes the treatment result on the back. Mia revises the card into a second version based on both technicians’ notes.

By the end of the term, Mia rotates through first-pass inspection, while complex mechanical adjustments are still reviewed by senior technicians. She writes that day’s observation for one instrument into the shared repair log and places the second-version card back beside the leak light. A new line on the back now carries another technician’s date and follow-up result.
articles.overall: A community of practice involves sustained participation in a shared domain, mutual learning, and experience becoming part of reusable, revisable shared practice. A newcomer begins with real but limited participation and can gradually contribute observations back into shared tools.
explanationParagraphs: Woodwind repair is their shared domain, weekly return cases keep them interacting, and the common log preserves ways of working that they continue to use. Mia takes part in observation and recording; several technicians then use, annotate, and revise her draft card. Her participation grows from completing a small task to helping improve the tools used by the group.

This is not a universal diagnostic method acquired from one lesson. The card records locally reviewable experience, complex judgments still go to qualified technicians, and the specific instrument still requires follow-up observation.

module.intro: Look at how people in the same domain keep working through problems together, and how a newcomer’s observations enter tools that others use and revise.
module.diagramTitle: How One Intermittent Problem Enters the Repair Room’s Shared Practice
diagramSteps: Let the newcomer take on a limited but real leak-check task
Try the reported action together with experienced members
Write the observation back into the existing shared repair log
Combine the new case with older records into a reusable draft card
Have multiple members use it, add exceptions, and continue review
diagramStepNotes: The repair room had maintained a shared repair log for years before Mia joined.
The static check shows no obvious continuous leak; a thin line is observed once on the fifth repetition.
The same observation is written on the repair sheet and copied into the shared log; the school is asked to keep observing.
Mia combines the new record with older cases into a draft card for reproduction, timing, and handoff.
Two senior technicians actually use and annotate it, and Mia revises it into a second version.
mapping: Shared repair log → shared practice that existed before Mia arrived.
Leak light → a real tool through which a newcomer participates.
This returning clarinet → the concrete event through which new experience enters existing practice.
Second-version card with multiple annotations → a newcomer’s contribution being adopted and revised by others.
module.boundary: This fictional repair scene illustrates shared participation, recording, and feedback. Actual instruments still require technical standards, professional qualifications, and case-specific review; one observation cannot become a universal diagnostic rule. A community’s experience can also be wrong and needs continued checking and correction from external evidence.
module.reflection: When a newcomer’s observation is actually used, modified, and written back into a shared tool by experienced members, how is that different from simply receiving one lesson from a mentor?

references.citation: Lave, J., & Wenger, E. (1991). Situated Learning: Legitimate Peripheral Participation. Cambridge University Press.
references.use: Supports the original framework of learning through participation in social practice and newcomers gradually taking part in real work; not every informal group is treated as a community of practice.

references.citation: Wenger-Trayner, E., & Wenger-Trayner, B. (2015, April 15). Communities of practice: a brief introduction.
references.use: Supports the authors’ explanation of the combination of domain, community, and shared practice, and of sustained interaction creating experience, tools, and ways of handling problems.

articles.titleZh: 那支偶尔失声的单簧管
articles.summaryZh: 一支学生单簧管第二次送回维修室：静态检查几乎正常，低音却偶尔发不出。米娅拿着漏气灯，第一次跟着老技师尝试重现这个具体问题。
storyParagraphsZh: 第三周，一支学生单簧管第二次送到米娅手里，标签写“低音偶尔发不出”。新来的米娅用漏气灯检查垫片接触，静态检查时却没有明显持续漏光。她把检查位置写在对应维修单上，没法只凭这张单告诉学校，那个偶尔发不出的音到底怎么了。
学区维修室多年来每周二一起处理各校木管乐器，长桌旁的共同维修簿记着三名技师的返修现象、处理动作和复查结果。米娅第一周只负责漏气检查这一小段。负责机械的老技师接过这支乐器的维修单，请她照学生描述重复同一组按键动作；他在另一侧观察联动，另一名技师记录异常出现的时点。
第五遍操作时，一个连接键有一次回位比前几次慢，漏气灯只在那一瞬出现细线。技师根据本次观察清洁并调整这支乐器的联动部位，随后三人再次重复同样动作和静态检查。维修单写下“本次观察：第五遍动作时出现细线”，同样记录被抄进共同维修簿；他们也请学校继续观察使用情况。
之后几周，米娅仍从漏气灯检查做起，但共同维修簿让她能看到老成员过去如何记录“持续出现”和“只有特定动作出现”的不同个案。她把这支单簧管的新记录和几条旧记录整理成一张草卡：先尝试重现报修动作，再记录观察时点，之后交给对应技师判断下一步；末尾留实际处理和复查栏。
老技师把草卡拿到长桌边试用，并补了一条：“若静态检查已经持续出现明显异常，直接按现象交对应技师，不必强行重复报修动作。”另一名技师随后在一件间歇问题上用这张卡记录时点，并把自己的处理结果写回背面。米娅根据两人的回写改了第二版。
学期末，米娅已经轮值第一轮检查，复杂机械调整仍由资深技师复核。她把当天一支乐器的观察写进共同维修簿，再把第二版小卡放回漏气灯旁；卡背面新添的一栏刚写上另一位技师的日期和复查结果。
articles.overallZh: 实践共同体是在共同领域中持续参与、相互学习，并让经验进入可复用、可修订的共享实践。新人从真实但有限的参与开始，也能逐步把自己的观察回馈给共同工具。
explanationParagraphsZh: 木管维修是这组人的共同领域，每周一起处理返修维持了交流，共同维修簿保存他们会继续使用的做法。米娅参加观察和记录，草卡又被几名技师实际采用、回写和修订；这让她的参与从完成小任务，延伸到改进大家的工具。
这不是一次师傅指导就获得通用诊断法。卡片只记录本室可复查经验，复杂问题仍交专业技师，具体乐器结果也需后续观察。

moduleZh.intro: 留意同一领域的人怎样持续一起处理问题，以及新人的观察怎样进入大家会使用和修改的共同工具。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 一次间歇问题怎样进入维修室的共同实践
diagramSteps: 新人先承担有限但真实的漏气检查
与老成员尝试重现同一返修现象
把本次观察写回已有共同维修簿
结合旧记录整理可复用草卡
由多人试用、补例外并继续复核
diagramStepNotes: 维修室在米娅加入前已有多年共同维修簿。
本次静态无明显持续漏光，第五遍动作时观察到一次细线。
同一观察写在维修单并抄进共同维修簿，请学校继续观察。
米娅用新记录和旧个案整理重现、记录、转交的草卡。
两名资深技师实际使用并回写，米娅据此改成第二版。
mapping: 共同维修簿 → 米娅加入前就存在的共享实践。
漏气灯 → 新成员承担真实任务的工具。
这支返修单簧管 → 新经验进入既有实践的具体事件。
多人回写的第二版小卡 → 新人贡献被共同采用并修订。
moduleZh.boundary: 这段虚构维修场景只说明共同参与、记录和回写。具体乐器仍需按技术标准、专业资格和个案复核来处理；一次观察不能成为通用诊断规则。实践共同体的经验也可能出错，需要继续检查并接受外部证据纠正。
moduleZh.reflection: 当一个新成员的观察被老成员实际采用、修改并写回共同工具时，这与“只是被师傅教了一次”有什么不同？

referencesZh.citation: Lave, J., & Wenger, E. (1991). Situated Learning: Legitimate Peripheral Participation. Cambridge University Press.
referencesZh.use: 支持通过参与社会实践学习以及新成员逐渐参与真实工作的原始著作框架；不把所有非正式群体都等同于实践共同体。

referencesZh.citation: Wenger-Trayner, E., & Wenger-Trayner, B. (2015, April 15). Communities of practice: a brief introduction.
referencesZh.use: 支持领域、共同体与共享实践三者结合，以及长期互动形成经验、工具和处理问题方法的作者说明。

articles.title: The €49 Item in the Yellow Returns Tray
articles.summary: The returns batch must go to finance before 15:00. Qi An has already checked a €49 bedding return but gets stuck on one question: who clicks “approve” first, and who receives the item first?
storyParagraphs: At 13:40, Qi An receives an unopened €49 bedding return. Finance will lock the day’s standard refund batch at 15:00. The order, seal, and customer request are all complete. He knows how to check orders and use the refund system. His onboarding role sheet says, “Standard returns with complete evidence up to €50 are approved by the returns coordinator,” but the handover never explained whether approval or warehouse receipt comes first, or what counts as complete for the day.

Qi An takes the required photos, puts the bedding into the yellow tray, and first asks the warehouse whether it can receive the item. The warehouse colleague says that goods fit for resale cannot enter the resale area until the system status reads “approved.” Qi An, however, worries that he is supposed to wait for the warehouse to verify the seal first, so he pushes the tray over. The warehouse sends it back to returns with a sticky note reading “awaiting approval.”

At 14:45, the supervisor notices that the tray is still there. She pulls out the old role sheet and points to Qi An’s existing approval authority for returns up to €50. She then explains the store’s daily sequence: Qi An verifies the evidence and approves first, hands the item to the warehouse by 14:30 for receipt, and only after warehouse receipt can it enter the 15:00 finance refund queue. The 14:30 cutoff applies only to the day’s refund batch; the warehouse continues its other work afterward.

The bedding has already missed that day’s batch and is placed on the overnight returns rack. The next morning, Qi An checks the order and seal again, clicks “approve” in the system, and hands the item to the warehouse. Once received, it moves into the resale area, and the finance system shows “entered today’s refund queue.” The customer then receives a notice that processing has entered the refund workflow, not a notification that money has already arrived.

At 14:10 that afternoon, a €65 vase arrives with a damaged edge. Qi An checks the order and photographs the damage. The amount exceeds his standard approval range, and the damage needs examination, so he routes approval to the supervisor and has warehouse quality control sign the vase into the “pending determination” rack. Only the photo folder and handoff number remain in the yellow tray, ready for the supervisor to continue the case.

At 15:00, finance locks the day’s standard refund batch. The €49 bedding is already in the resale area, with its queue number visible in the system. The €65 vase remains on quality control’s “pending determination” rack, and the yellow-tray label reads “supervisor approval in progress.” Qi An clips the old “awaiting approval” note into the handover book and writes 14:30 and 15:00 beside it.
articles.overall: Role clarity means knowing the scope of an existing role, what counts as completion, the handoff sequence, and the escalation path for exceptions. Even when authority already exists, unclear expectations can still produce reasonable mutual waiting.
explanationParagraphs: Authority to approve standard returns up to €50 was already written in the role sheet. What was unclear was the sequence among approval, warehouse receipt, and the 15:00 finance batch. Once clarified, the same €49 item is completed under the existing authority.

The damaged €65 vase moves to the supervisor and quality control, showing that clarity changes the decision path rather than creating new authority, removing review, or forcing every case through the same route.

module.intro: Compare the existing authority, completion standard, handoff times, and exception path for a task to see what each person is waiting for before taking it over.
module.diagramTitle: How the €49 Bedding Moves from Mutual Waiting into the Refund Queue
diagramSteps: Receive a standard return under existing responsibility
Create back-and-forth because approval and warehouse-receipt order are unclear
Use the old role sheet to clarify authority and add a completion standard
Complete the same item the next day through approval → receipt → finance queue
Route the damaged €65 item to supervisor and quality control as an exception
diagramStepNotes: The original sheet already assigns complete-evidence standard returns ≤€50 to the returns coordinator.
Qi An waits for warehouse verification first, while the warehouse waits for system approval.
14:30 is the receipt cutoff for that day’s refund batch, and finance locks the batch at 15:00; it is not the end of warehouse operations.
The customer receives notice that the item entered the refund process, not confirmation that funds have arrived.
The €65 vase arriving at 14:10 is signed into the pending-determination rack by quality control while supervisor approval continues.
mapping: Old role sheet → evidence that the authority already existed.
Yellow tray moving back and forth → mutual waiting caused by an unclear completion boundary.
14:30 / 15:00 → this store’s fictional handoff and finance-batch times.
Pending-determination rack + handoff number → the exception follows a different path while responsibility remains continuous.
module.boundary: Role clarity cannot solve insufficient skill, inadequate resources, or an unreasonable underlying system, and it does not permanently freeze responsibilities. When amounts, evidence, or tasks change, role boundaries and escalation paths may also need revision.
module.reflection: If authority is already written in the role description but two sides still wait for each other, what receiving conditions and cutoffs would you check, and how would you confirm that both sides agree on what counts as complete?

references.citation: Rizzo, J. R., House, R. J., & Lirtzman, S. I. (1970). Role Conflict and Ambiguity in Complex Organizations. Administrative Science Quarterly, 15(2), 150–163.
references.use: Supports the original measurement research on role ambiguity and role conflict while keeping the two concepts distinct.

references.citation: Health and Safety Executive. Management Standards – Role.
references.use: Supports practical guidance on clarifying work requirements, responsibilities, and routes for responding to uncertainty; it is not treated as a legal requirement for all organizations worldwide.

articles.titleZh: 黄色托盘里的四十九欧元
articles.summaryZh: 下午三点前，退货批次要交财务。齐安已经把一件49欧元床品核完，却卡在“谁先点批准、谁先收货”这一步。
storyParagraphsZh: 下午一点四十，齐安收到一件49欧元未拆封床品退货，财务三点就要锁定当日标准退款批次。订单、封条和顾客申请都齐全，他会查订单，也熟悉退款系统。入职资料里的职责清单其实写着“证据齐全的标准退货≤50欧元由退货协调员审批”，但交接时没人说明审批与仓库接收谁先、什么时候才算当天完成。
齐安拍完照片，把床品放进黄色托盘，先问仓库能否点收。仓库同事说，可再售商品要等系统状态变成“已批准”才能入格；齐安却担心自己应先等仓库确认封条，于是把托盘推过去。仓库又把托盘送回退货区，附上“待审批”便签。
两点四十五，主管看到托盘还在，翻出那张旧职责清单，指给齐安看≤50欧元的审批范围。她再把本店当天批次顺序说清：齐安先核证据并批准，14:30前交仓库点收，仓库接收后才能进入15:00财务退款队列。14:30只是当天退款批次的退货接收截点，仓库其他工作仍继续。
这件床品已经错过当天批次，被放进退货区的隔夜架。第二天上午，齐安按清单重新核订单和封条，系统点“批准”，仓库接收后把商品移到可再售格；财务系统显示“已进入今日退款队列”。顾客随后收到的是处理已进入退款流程的通知，而不是到账通知。
下午两点十分，又来一只65欧元、边缘破损的花瓶。齐安先核订单并拍照，看到金额高于自己的标准审批范围，破损情况也需要核查，便把审批转给主管，同时让仓库质检签收实物到“待判定”架。黄色托盘里只留下照片夹和转交编号，主管可以接着处理。
下午三点，财务锁定当天标准退款批次。49欧元床品已在可再售格，系统里显示队列编号；65欧元花瓶仍在质检的“待判定”架，黄色托盘标签写着“主管审批中”。齐安把那张旧“待审批”便签夹回交接本，旁边补写14:30和15:00两个时点。
articles.overallZh: 角色清晰度让成员知道已有职责范围、完成标准、交接顺序和例外升级路径。即使权限已经存在，若这些预期没有说清，也可能出现合理的相互等待。
explanationParagraphsZh: ≤50欧元标准退货审批权原本就在职责清单中；真正模糊的是批准、仓库接收和15:00财务批次的顺序。澄清后，同一49欧元床品按既有权限完成。
65欧元破损花瓶转主管和质检，说明清晰度改变的是选择路径，不是新增权限、取消复核或让所有案件走同一流程。

moduleZh.intro: 对照一项工作的已有权限、完成标准、交接时间和例外路径，查清每个人接手前在等什么。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 49欧元床品怎样从相互等待进入退款队列
diagramSteps: 按已有职责收到标准退货
因审批与仓库接收顺序不清形成往返
用旧职责清单澄清权限并补充完成标准
次日按批准→接收→财务队列完成同一件床品
65欧元破损件按例外路径转主管与质检
diagramStepNotes: 原清单已写≤50欧元、证据齐全的标准退货由协调员审批。
齐安等仓库先验，仓库等系统先批准。
14:30是当天退款批次接收截点，15:00财务锁批，并非仓库停止工作。
顾客收到的是“进入退款流程”通知，不是到账确认。
14:10到达的65欧元花瓶由质检签收到待判定架，主管继续审批。
mapping: 旧职责清单 → 证明权限早已存在。
黄色托盘往返 → 完成边界不清造成的相互等待。
14:30/15:00 → 本店虚构的当天交接与财务批次时点。
待判定架＋转交编号 → 例外件改变路径但保持责任连续。
moduleZh.boundary: 角色清晰并不能解决能力不足、资源短缺或制度本身不合理的问题，也不等于把责任永久固定。金额、证据或任务变化时，角色边界和升级路径仍可能需要更新。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果权限早已写在职责里，但两边仍互相等待，你会查看各自的接收条件和时间截点，并怎样确认双方对“完成”理解一致？

referencesZh.citation: Rizzo, J. R., House, R. J., & Lirtzman, S. I. (1970). Role Conflict and Ambiguity in Complex Organizations. Administrative Science Quarterly, 15(2), 150–163.

articles.title: The Square Would Not Drop Free
articles.summary: Forty display panels are due on Monday. The new boards are as thick as the old ones, but the first square Cen Yue cuts with the old settings stays attached to the test strip, its edge darker than before.
storyParagraphs: A woodworking studio must deliver forty custom display panels on Monday. For the previous two years, it has used 3 mm birch plywood, and Cen Yue’s standard settings card has been stable on the same machine. On Friday, the new material arrives: 40 production boards, 1 separate first-article board, and 3 test strips from the same batch. The supplier identifies the material as a 3 mm bamboo-veneer composite and notes that its surface and core construction differ from the old birch board.

Cen Yue starts with test strip A, cutting a small square in the machine’s test mode with the old birch settings. Fibers remain connected at two places on the back, and the edge is darker than on the old board. He writes the batch number and both observations on the back, then puts the supplier’s description beside the old card and compares it with the words “birch plywood.” All 40 production boards stay on the rack.

The machine manual lists speed and air assist as separately testable controls. Cen Yue knows that, at unchanged power, slower movement means longer exposure along each part of the cut. But A’s edge is already dark, so full separation is not the only result he must watch. For strip B, he keeps power and air assist unchanged and lowers speed to the adjacent test setting. B drops free, but its edge is darker. He places it beside A and records both the gain and the cost of that change.

For strip C, he keeps B’s power and speed and changes only air assist to the adjacent setting allowed by the machine. C also drops free, with a lighter edge than B. Cen Yue lays the three strips out in order and labels each with its machine settings and observed results. More than twenty minutes have passed, and all three test strips are used. He clips the record beside the first-article board before picking up the customer drawing.

Cen Yue then uses the one separate first-article board under condition C to cut the complete customer shape. He checks full separation, edge condition, hole positions, dimensions, and fit with the stand. He signs the first-article record before starting the 40 delivery boards. During production, each piece is checked after removal for complete separation and edge condition; dimensions are spot-checked at the studio’s existing batch checkpoints. Any abnormality stops the run and sends him back to the record.

Before shipment on Monday, all 40 finished panels are boxed. The new settings card reads “3 mm bamboo-veneer composite / first article confirmed for this batch,” while the old birch card remains intact. Test strips A, B, and C and the first-article record are stapled together and returned to the process binder beside the machine; the batch-inspection sheet is filed behind them.
articles.overall: Adaptive expertise combines efficient, skilled performance with understanding why a method works. When conditions change, people can use prior knowledge and resources for further learning to make informed adjustments, rather than merely repeating old steps or trying changes at random.
explanationParagraphs: The old settings had been reliable for birch plywood. Comparing the new material description, Cen Yue knows that equal thickness alone does not justify copying the old card. He uses his understanding of speed and exposure time to choose the first adjustment, checking both separation and edge darkening.

Changing one control at a time is the method used to distinguish results in this small test, not the definition of adaptive expertise. A/B/C, the first article, and the batch checks support a processing choice only for this machine and material batch; they do not establish settings that work under every condition.

module.intro: Identify why the old method worked and which conditions have changed, then use prior knowledge and resources for learning to adjust it. In this example, small tests and a first-article check connect the adjustment back to the real order.
module.diagramTitle: How A, B, and C Support This Batch of Bamboo-Veneer Composite
diagramSteps: Use the old birch settings on A to establish a baseline
Use the material change and machine test controls to let B change speed only
Keep B’s conditions for C and change air assist only
Use a separate first article to check the full delivery standard
Produce under the new card while keeping the existing batch-quality checks
diagramStepNotes: A does not fully separate and has a darker edge; the 40 production boards remain untouched.
B keeps power and air assist unchanged and lowers speed to the adjacent test setting; exposure lasts longer, the square separates, but the edge becomes darker.
C keeps B’s power and speed and changes only the machine-permitted air-assist test setting.
The first article checks full separation, edge, holes, dimensions, and fit before sign-off.
During production, separation and edge condition are checked piece by piece and dimensions are spot-checked at existing batch points; abnormalities stop the run.
mapping: Supplier material description → evidence that the material condition covered by the old settings has changed.
A/B/C test strips → the evidence chain from changing one control at a time in this test.
Separate first-article board → connects the small test back to the customer’s full delivery standard.
Old card alongside the new batch card → preserves established expertise while limiting the new method’s scope.
module.boundary: Adaptive expertise does not require reinventing the process every time; well-practiced methods can remain useful where they still fit. This is a fictional machine-and-material scenario and does not provide real laser-processing parameters or safety guidance. One A/B/C test sequence cannot establish universal causation; the new card applies only within the range supported by this batch’s first article and production checks.
module.reflection: When a familiar method meets new conditions, can you explain why it originally worked? What knowledge or learning resources would help you decide which steps to keep, which to adjust, and what evidence to use to check the result?

articles.summaryZh: 四十块展示牌周一要交。新板和旧板一样厚，岑越按旧卡切的第一个方框却还连在测试片上，边缘也深了一圈。
storyParagraphsZh: 木作工作室周一要交四十块定制展示牌。过去两年一直用3毫米桦木夹板，岑越的标准参数卡在同一台设备上很稳定。周五新材料到货：40块交付板、1块首件样板和3条同批测试片。供应商把材料标为3毫米竹皮复合板，并注明表层和芯材组合与旧桦木板不同。
岑越先拿测试片A，用旧桦木参数在设备的测试模式切一个小方框。A背面有两处纤维仍连着，边缘也比旧板深。他在背面写下批次号和这两个现象，把供应商说明放到旧卡旁边，对照卡上的“桦木夹板”。料架上的40块正式板没有动。
设备手册把速度和空气辅助列为可单独测试的控制项。岑越知道，功率不变时，走得慢些会让切缝每段受作用的时间更长；但A的边缘已经偏深，切透之外还得留意焦色。他拿测试片B，保持功率和空气辅助不变，只把速度调慢到相邻测试档。B完整脱落，边缘却更深。他把B排在A旁，记下这次换来的好处和代价。
测试片C保持B的功率和速度，只把空气辅助改到设备允许的相邻测试档。C同样完整脱落，边缘比B浅。岑越把三条测试片按A、B、C排开，逐一补上机器档位和观察结果。二十多分钟已经过去，三条测试材料也都用了；他先把记录夹到首件样板旁，再拿起客户图纸。
岑越随后用那1块独立首件样板按C条件切完整客户图形，核对切透、边缘、孔位、尺寸和与支架的装配。他在首件记录上签字，才开始动40块交付板。批量生产时，每块取下后都检查是否完整分离和边缘状态，并按工作室原有批次节点做尺寸抽查；异常就停机回到记录。
周一出货前，40块成品全部装箱。新参数卡写着“3毫米竹皮复合板／本批首件确认”，旧桦木卡没有被覆盖。A、B、C三条测试片和首件记录订在一起，放回设备旁的工艺夹；批次检查页也夹在同一份记录后面。
articles.overallZh: 适应性专长把熟练有效的操作与对做法为何有效的理解结合起来。条件变化时，人能利用已有知识和可供学习的资源作出有依据的调整，而不只是重复旧步骤或随意尝试。
explanationParagraphsZh: 旧参数在桦木板上长期有效。岑越对照新材料说明，知道不能仅凭厚度相同就照搬旧卡；他再用速度与作用时间的关系选择第一步试验，并同时检查切透和焦边。
一次只改变一个控制项，是这次小试用来分辨结果的办法，不是适应性专长的定义。A/B/C、首件和批次检查只支持这台设备与这一批材料的处理选择，不能保证参数对其他条件普遍有效。

moduleZh.intro: 辨认旧做法为何有效、哪些条件已变，再利用已有知识和学习资源作出调整。本例用小试与首件核对，把调整接回真实订单。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: A、B、C测试片怎样支持这一批竹皮复合板
diagramSteps: 用旧桦木参数在A上建立基线
依据材料变化和设备测试项选择B只改速度
C保持B条件并只改空气辅助
用独立首件核对完整交付标准
按新卡生产并执行原有批次质量检查
diagramStepNotes: A未完全切透且边缘偏深，40块正式板未动。
B保持功率和空气辅助，只调慢到相邻速度测试档；作用时间更长，切透了，但边缘更深。
C保持B功率和速度，只改设备允许的空气辅助测试档。
首件核对切透、边缘、孔位、尺寸和装配后才签字。
批量时逐件看分离/边缘，并按原节点抽查尺寸；异常即停。
mapping: 供应商材料说明 → 证明旧参数的材料条件已变化。
A/B/C测试片 → 一次只改变一个控制项的本次证据链。
独立首件样板 → 把小试接回客户交付标准。
旧卡与本批新卡并存 → 保留熟练经验并限定新方法范围。
moduleZh.boundary: 适应性专长不要求每次重造流程，仍适用的熟练做法可以保留。这是虚构设备和材料情境，不提供真实激光加工参数或安全建议。一次A/B/C小试不能证明普遍因果，新卡只适用于经本批首件和生产检查支持的范围。
moduleZh.reflection: 当熟悉做法遇到新条件时，你能说明它原本为何有效吗？你会借助哪些知识或学习资源，判断哪些步骤可保留、哪些需要调整，并用什么证据检验？
